key_insight: A retrieval-guided noise optimization process steers diffusion-based motion generation using examples from a motion database, enabling zero-shot satisfaction of very tight spatiotemporal constraints (e.g., narrow obstacle courses, exact step counts).
problem_solved: Current motion generators fail on highly-constrained tasks with severe spatial/temporal restrictions; this work enables reliable generation that meets such customized constraints without task-specific retraining.
method: Retrieve relevant motion snippets or priors from a dataset conditioned on the user-specified goal/constraint.
Optimize the diffusion sampling noise using information from retrieved examples to bias generation toward constraint-satisfying regions of motion space.
Combine retrieval-guided noise shaping with the diffusion model’s sampling loop and constraint-aware objective to produce feasible, diverse motions zero-shot.
impact: Makes generative motion models practical for strict control scenarios in character animation, robotics, and virtual agents by improving success rates on hard constraints while preserving diversity and zero-shot generalization.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: retrieval → noise optimization → diffusion sampler → final motion
Before/after motion sequences overlaid on an environment with obstacles/step markers to show constraint compliance
Success-rate chart comparing baseline diffusion vs retrieval-guided approach across increasingly tight constraints
Ablation table/heatmap showing contribution of retrieval and noise-optimization components to performance
paper_title: Towards Highly-Constrained Human Motion Generation with Retrieval-Guided Diffusion Noise Optimization
paper_authors: Hanchao Liu, Fang-Lue Zhang, Shining Zhang, Tai-Jiang Mu, Shi-Min Hu
